# [TASK] Self-healing read-through: treat schema-drifted MongoDB documents as cache misses

## Task
Movie documents persisted under an older schema (e.g. `spokenLanguages` as `List<String>` before ADR-010's `List<SpokenLanguage>`) made the read-through path throw a 500 instead of degrading — and kept throwing on every retry, since a failed read never reaches save-through to repair it. Fix: treat an unreadable persisted document as a cache miss.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A document persisted in an outdated shape no longer 500s on any endpoint (native or facade) — all `findByTmdbId` call sites route through one `findPersistedMovie` seam that catches the conversion error, evicts, and returns empty so the caller re-fetches from TMDB
- [x] The document is replaced with a current-shape document on next access, confirmed live in MongoDB (count stays 1 — replaced, not duplicated)
- [x] Only mapping/conversion failures are absorbed; genuine infrastructure failures (`DataAccessException`) still propagate and nothing is deleted — unit-tested
- [x] Unit test (conversion error -> re-fetch) and Testcontainers integration test (real malformed MongoDB document healed end-to-end) both green — 6 new tests, 117/117 passing
- [x] [ADR-011](../blob/main/docs/architecture/adr/011-self-healing-read-through-on-schema-drift.md) written; verified live through the gateway and via the Postman/newman collection (folder 12)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 7

## Notes
Scoped to movie-service only — actor-service and user-service are PostgreSQL with Flyway/`ddl-auto: validate`, which already catches drift at startup, so the same pattern there would be dead code. This pattern only applies to re-derivable (TMDB-sourced) data; user-owned data must never adopt it, since it can't be re-fetched from anywhere.
